task_1.title: Restore correct label-to-bin mapping in groupby_bins
task_1.description: The update fixes a regression in labeled bin grouping so that xarray `groupby_bins` results use the correct user-supplied label for each bin. Aggregations, mapped operations, and group access now follow bin order rather than an incorrect reordered label mapping, including for string labels and custom label orderings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `groupby_bins` returns and exposes groups using the correct correspondence between each bin and its supplied label, so labeled bin aggregations and label-based group access produce the expected subset and counts.

expectation.grounded: When `xarray.DataArray.groupby_bins` is called with `labels`, the grouped result must preserve the semantic mapping between each bin produced by `pandas.cut` and the matching label in bin order. This must hold for reduction operations such as `.sum()` and `.count()`, for `.map(...)`, for string labels, numeric labels, and explicitly non-sorted label sequences. The resulting grouped coordinate values and any label-based access through the group mapping must refer to the subset belonging to that label's bin, not a reordered or alphabetically sorted label assignment.
expectation.conceptual: Providing labels for bin-based grouping should behave exactly as users expect: each output group should represent the data that falls into that labeled bin. The library should not reshuffle labels based on lexical or numeric sorting, and all grouped operations should stay consistent with the visible labels.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not change existing `groupby_bins` behavior for unlabeled binning beyond retaining equivalence with `pandas.cut` output. It must continue to work with both `use_flox=True` and `use_flox=False`, preserve correct behavior for `include_lowest` variations, keep original array dimensions unchanged after grouping operations, and continue to support ellipsis-based reductions on grouped arrays.
constraints.conceptual: The correction should be limited to the label-to-bin correspondence bug and should not introduce regressions in ordinary bin grouping, backend choice, or standard grouped reductions.

behavior: `groupby_bins(..., labels=...)` now associates observed groups with labels according to bin position rather than sorted label value.
String labels produce counts and subsets for the intended bins instead of being mismatched by alphabetical ordering.
Custom label orderings remain intact and are reflected consistently in grouped aggregation results.
Numeric labels continue to work as explicit output labels for grouped results.
Grouped `.sum()`, `.count()`, and `.map(...)` results remain aligned with `pandas.cut`-based expectations.
The corrected behavior is consistent whether flox-based grouping is enabled or disabled.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray is grouped with `groupby_bins` using explicit string labels, each label should identify the subset of data that falls into its corresponding bin.
When labels are supplied in a non-sorted order, grouped results should preserve that intended label-to-bin mapping instead of reordering by label value.
When `.sum()` is applied to a labeled `groupby_bins` result, the output coordinates and aggregated values should match the equivalent grouping produced via `pandas.cut`.
When `.map(lambda x: x.sum())` is applied to a labeled `groupby_bins` result, it should produce the same label-aligned output as direct grouped reduction.

When `.count()` is applied to a labeled binned grouping over sparse or partially empty bins, each reported count should correspond to the correct labeled bin and empty bins should remain representable as missing or empty outcomes where applicable.
When grouping is executed with either flox enabled or disabled, observable labeled bin results should be equivalent.
When unlabeled binning is used, standard `groupby_bins` aggregations should continue to agree with `pandas.cut` semantics.

task_2.title: Document xarray string accessor examples and clarified behavior
task_2.description: The 2023.4.2 update expands user-facing documentation for xarray string accessors by adding concrete examples for common string transformation, classification, matching, and padding methods, and by clarifying the documented behavior of case folding and lowercase output naming. The change improves discoverability and interpretation of existing APIs without changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the xarray string accessor documentation clearly demonstrates how representative string methods behave on DataArray inputs, including case conversion, character classification, prefix and suffix matching, counting, and padding, so users can reliably understand expected outputs and edge cases when upgrading.

expectation.grounded: The public documentation for xarray.core.accessor_str.StringAccessor should include usable examples for methods such as capitalize, lower, swapcase, title, upper, casefold, isalnum, isalpha, isdecimal, isdigit, islower, isnumeric, isspace, istitle, isupper, count, startswith, endswith, and pad. The documented contract should show that these methods return DataArray-shaped results of the same shape as the input or broadcast shape where applicable, including boolean arrays for classification methods, integer arrays for count, and string arrays for transformations and padding. The documented behavior of StringAccessor.casefold should explicitly distinguish case folding from lowercasing for language-specific characters, and the lower method documentation should refer to the returned value consistently as lowered.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to consult the library documentation and see clear, concrete examples of what common string accessor operations return, including transformed strings, boolean checks, counts, and broadcasted outputs. The documentation should also make clear that case folding can differ from ordinary lowercase conversion for some characters.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade should not alter the runtime semantics, signatures, return types, broadcasting behavior, or error behavior of existing StringAccessor methods. Existing string operations must continue to behave as before; the update is limited to public documentation clarity and observable examples.
constraints.conceptual: The release must improve understanding without changing how existing string APIs work in practice. Existing user code should continue to run the same way after the upgrade.

behavior: String transformation methods are documented as returning string-valued DataArray results aligned to the input shape.
String classification methods are documented as returning boolean DataArray results with the same shape as the evaluated strings.
StringAccessor.count is documented to support string or regex patterns and array-like patterns that broadcast against the source array.
StringAccessor.pad is documented to support left, right, and both-side padding, including array-like width and fill character inputs that broadcast.
StringAccessor.casefold is documented to normalize case more aggressively than lowercase conversion for certain language-specific characters.
The lower method documentation now consistently names its returned result as lowered.
acceptance_criteria: When users read the string accessor documentation, they should find concrete examples for the documented transformation, classification, matching, count, and padding methods.
When users consult StringAccessor.casefold documentation, it should describe that case folding may produce different results than lowercasing for some characters.
When users consult the count and pad documentation, it should show that array-like arguments can produce broadcasted DataArray outputs.
When users upgrade from 2023.4.1 to 2023.4.2, existing calls to documented string accessor methods should behave the same at runtime.
When users read the lower method documentation, the return description should consistently use the corrected lowered terminology.
